What’s It Like to Be Tennis’s World Number One? Daniil Medvedev Lets Us Into the Club

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1182 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The ATP Finals—the most notable men’s tournament on the tennis calendar outside of the Grand Slams—kicked off on Sunday in Torino.
  • It has been revealed that ranking, of course, is everything—it’s what gets you invited to the finals—and the summa achievement of the world’s top ranking is the subject of a new book, ATP No.
  • We sat down with one of those iconic players—Medvedev, one of the five current or former number-ones still competing—to ask him, you know, what it’s like to do something better than anyone else in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The ATP Finals—the most notable men’s tournament on the tennis calendar outside of the Grand Slams—kicked off on Sunday in Torino. Founded in 1970 as a season-ending competition pitting the highest-ranked players against each other, the current iteration features the world’s top eight men—Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe, and Rafael Jodar—facing each other first in a round-robin group format and then in elimination stages. (It’s similar in format to the women’s WTA Finals, which concluded Sunday in Indian Wells, with Mirra Andreeva taking home the massive trophy.).

It has been revealed that ranking, of course, is everything—it’s what gets you invited to the finals—and the summa achievement of the world’s top ranking is the subject of a new book, ATP No. 1 Club: Icons of Men’s Tennis, just out from Phaidon. It features iconic photos of each number-one player since 1973—the men’s game has seen only 30, including Alcaraz, Zverev, and Medvedev—along with text by the late award-winning tennis writer Mark Hodgkinson.

We sat down with one of those iconic players—Medvedev, one of the five current or former number-ones still competing—to ask him, you know, what it’s like to do something better than anyone else in the world.

Vogue: Do you remember, from your earliest years playing tennis, who was number one at the time?

According to recent reports, daniil Medvedev: I started playing tennis when I was six, in 2002, but I was not yet a tennis fan, let’s say. By the time I started to understand tennis a bit more, Roger [Federer] was there already, and I think for most of my childhood it was Roger at number one, and then Rafa, who from time to time took the top spot. And then came Novak—who, as we know now, took the leading spot for a longer period of time. One time, years later, I made a game of it—I think I named, not all of them, probably 27 of them.

Did you have a tennis hero when you were a kid?

So I have to be honest here: I’m still probably a bit like this, but when I was young, whoever was winning too much—doesn’t matter which sport—I stopped liking them. I’m like, Okay, he’s only winning. So at one point I was supporting anyone against Roger—I don’t say it in a bad way, it’s just how I am. At one moment it was Barcelona with [their former coach] Pep Guardiola and they were beating everyone, and I was like, Okay—give us something newly introduced.

It has been revealed that but it changed from tournament to tournament: I supported Marat [Safin in 2005] when he won the Australian Open. This was incredible—we, as kids in Russia, were waking up early in the morning to watch his matches. Andy Roddick—I loved his serve; sometimes I was copying it. Novak as well, when he just came in, before he started beating everyone and I was cheering for the underdog. I never had one hero.

It has been revealed that when you were dreaming kid dreams, was it about winning Wimbledon or another tournament? Was being the world number one ever part of that?

I never was thinking about number one or a Grand Slam. Of course, when I grew up and started playing better tennis, those kind of goals came into place. But when I was really young, I remember hitting against the wall, and because the wall never misses, I was thinking that I’m playing against Roger, Rafa, Novak. I was trying to beat them, but of course you cannot beat the wall. Those were fun memories—and I think, probably, in the back of my mind, I knew that if I’m playing them, it means that I’m somewhere in the top rankings.

My dream was to become a great tennis player, and I feel like I achieved it. I’m happy about it: Every day you go to practice, you work hard, you fight for the matches, and you don’t think about it. But when I talk to someone like you and put myself back there, I’m like, I actually achieved my dream. It’s just that the dream constantly changes, because you want more.

Did you feel different when you first became the ATP number one player in 2022?

It has been revealed that yes and no. Maybe there’s a tiny bit more pressure and attention paid to you, but it’s also just such a nice feeling. I mean, you are the best in the whole world, and everyone else is just trying. And it was not easy, but I made it. [Medvedev became the first player outside the so-called Big Four—Djokovic, Federer, Nadal, and Murray—to hold the top ranking in 18 years.].

Did that put a kind of target on you that hadn’t been there before?

For sure, especially in the world we live in now, that happens. Whenever you lose: “Oh, he’s not good enough to be world number one.” But I didn’t care, because I’m like, “I’m number one,” and it felt so good. People would ask me after a loss, “Maybe the ranking put more pressure on you? Maybe that’s why you didn’t perform.” I’d just say, “Maybe yes,” but I didn’t care. It was such a good feeling. Anyone who has been there, I think, will tell you the same: It’s a nice feeling. I want to try to be there again, of course—it’s going to be super tough, especially with Carlos and Jannik [Sinner] winning so much.

Did people—either inside or outside of tennis—treat you differently when you were number one? Did things come to you more easily?

For sure, when I was the world number one—I was on a big stretch of winning the 2021 US Open, playing some Masters finals, winning some Masters—I got some, whatever you call it, invitations. I remember going to Los Angeles before Indian Wells after I became world number one, and I went to some restaurants and I would ask for the bill and they’re like, “Yes—someone took care of it.” So stuff like this—when you are world number one, people talk a bit more about you; you’re on TV more. These are things which come with, let’s call it fame, which also can have a downside: Some people do this kind of thing just for pleasure, but maybe someone else pays and thinks that you’re going to sit and talk to him for 30 minutes. And I don’t want to be obliged to do something because someone did something for me—that’s just how I live. Especially if I’m rushing somewhere, you know: I’m okay to pay, man. As I say, there are some upsides, some downsides. If you get invited to a football match and you meet some players, or a baseball match: fun.

Baseball game—not a match, game.

Sources indicate that ah, game. Okay. I didn’t know this. In any case: I just enjoy life. I’m number one, I enjoy life. I’m number 10, I enjoy life.

This conversation has been edited and condensed.

Latest Update: Robert Pattinson Is the Next James Bond

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1008 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, after a whirlwind month of speculation, unsubstantiated rumors, and endless Kalshi prognostication, white smoke has finally emerged from the Amazon MGM chimney.
  • Recent findings suggest that the announcement ends the long-running—and quite frankly, exhausting—mystery over Daniel Craig’s successor and starts a fresh creative era for the 007 franchise, which Amazon acquired from longtime Bond custodians Michael G.
  • Sources indicate that “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after a whirlwind month of speculation, unsubstantiated rumors, and endless Kalshi prognostication, white smoke has finally emerged from the Amazon MGM chimney. There’s a upcoming James Bond—and his name is Robert Pattinson.

Recent findings suggest that the announcement ends the long-running—and quite frankly, exhausting—mystery over Daniel Craig’s successor and starts a fresh creative era for the 007 franchise, which Amazon acquired from longtime Bond custodians Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli in February 2025, four years after No Time to Die was released. Now, Pattinson will tux up as the seventh cinematic Bond under the stewardship of super-producers David Heyman and Amy Pascal and the vision of GQ’s Director of the Year Denis Villeneuve, marking arguably the biggest role of the 40-year-old London-born actor’s career.

Sources indicate that “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”.

According to recent reports, rumors of Pattinson’s selection caught fire in October, when delays on The Batman Part II gave him a window to audition for Bond at Berkshire’s Bray Studios, alongside peers Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden, and an unnamed fourth actor. The chatter heightened a couple weeks later when various British tabloids suggested that Turner, O’Connor, and Lowden were each the preferred choice to satisfy the demands and responsibilities of the beloved British action hero—heightening suspicion that a final decision was looming. According to THR, the finalists were judged “based on stunts, camera presence.” But Pattinson’s last-minute arrival clearly tipped the scale.

Industry observers note that “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007,” stated Villeneuve in a statement to THR. “I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our fresh James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”.

Industry observers note that it’s both a particularly inspired and obvious choice. Pattinson’s physical traits and characteristics hue close to Ian Fleming’s original Bond—tall and slim, with dark hair. He’s already a bona fide movie star, the current face of DC Studios’ Batman franchise; meanwhile, the selection catches him at the tail end of another booked-and-busy year. Unlike his auditioning peers, the acclaimed actor will enter the franchise well-experienced working in IP and with big-name directors. After co-leading this spring’s The Drama, he chewed up scenes as Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey (the second time working with Nolan after Tenet), made a creepy turn as Chris Hansen in Primetime, and will close 2026 as Scytale in Dune: Part 3—now the first of future Villeneuve collaborations, a relationship that surely helped him acquire his license to kill.

“James Bond is one of the most beloved, inspiring, iconic, and yet enigmatic characters in literature and movies,” Pascal and Heyman stated jointly to THR. “The legacy of this character is in great hands with Robert Pattinson. His fearlessness as an actor, his self-deprecating wit, and his ability to continually reinvent himself make him the perfect Bond for our times.”.

It has been revealed that the decision to hire a movie star isn’t a risky choice, but there’s not much precedent within the franchise—especially recently. When he succeeded Pierce Brosnan as Bond in 2005, beating out Clive Owen, Michael Fassbender, and Henry Cavill, Craig boasted an under-the-radar resume. He’d just come off Matthew Vaughn’s crime thriller Layer Cake, but otherwise had played supporting roles in Road to Perdition, The Mother, and Enduring Love. His only big-budget studio experience came several years earlier as Angelina Jolie’s love interest in Tomb Raider.

Naturally, the British press drew its fangs upon his selection, critiquing everything from his general obscurity to his physical features, which stood in stark contrast to previous Bond actors. “The Mane’s Blond, James Blond,” chirped The Irish Times, while The London Daily Mirror played with the same pun: “The Name’s Bland … James Bland.” At his official introduction to the press along the Thames, Craig arrived on a speedboat wearing a life vest, attracting instant mockery—the first of several digs about his less-than-sleek aesthetic and physical abilities. (One tabloid insulted an on-set sunburn and his inability to drive a stick shift car.).

Pattinson, however, has mostly conjured genuine excitement—not in spite of, but because of, his extreme familiarity with moviegoers, dating back to his Young Adult days in the Harry Potter and Twilight franchises. Since then, over the last decade-plus, his eccentric characters and commanding screen presence immediately qualifies him as someone “stirring and exciting and different,” descriptors that Pascal stated she prioritized in their methodical search.

Sources indicate that thanks to director Martin Campbell, Casino Royale returned the Bond franchise to earth and established Craig as a grounded, gritty action star in the mold of Jason Bourne. The movie ended up raking in $616 million globally, the highest earning Bond film to date, and debuted Craig into four more sequels. Similarly, Pattinson will have the benefit of a highly-respected, Oscar-nominated director in his corner with experience shepherding IP into new places and eliciting compelling performances about tortured male protagonists.

It has been revealed that with Villeneuve at the helm of this 26th installment, don’t expect another hard creative pivot; the man behind Prisoners, Blade Runner 2049, and Dune wasn’t hired to bring back the colorful, absurdist, gadget-heavy era that Austin Powers parodied throughout the 90’s. Still, new leadership means a new direction—a clean slate for Pattinson to burnish an already diverse, robust career and prove his chops again at the highest level of scrutiny.

Latest Update: Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta

📅 15 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (642 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mushroom fans: Bookmark this recipe immediately.
  • A few helpful notes for pasta success: (1) While any pasta will work, egg-based noodles, like the fettuccine I recommend here, are the best complement to the sauce.
  • Find more fall favorite meals here: Weeknight Pumpkin Chili; Cream-ish of Mushroom Soup; Mushrooms au Poivre.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mushroom fans: Bookmark this recipe immediately. It will give you everything you want when you crave a creamy mushroom pasta as soon as the crisp fall air sets in. The hardworking trio of miso, Parmesan, and touch of soy sauce delivers an umami bomb of flavor that doesn’t overwhelm, but magnifies, the best of earthy mushrooms. Coupled with luscious noodles enrobed in a creamy (but not heavy) sauce, what’s not to love?

A few helpful notes for pasta success: (1) While any pasta will work, egg-based noodles, like the fettuccine I recommend here, are the best complement to the sauce. The nests (Rummo and De Cecco are great accessible brands) cook far faster than standard straight pasta, almost as fast as fresh. (2) Don’t be afraid to season your mushrooms! Yes, I know this goes against all that we’ve learned about salting them too early in the cooking process, but just a bit of salt will get them going and releasing their water faster for eventual crisp-browned edges. Don’t be alarmed if you see a pool of water at the start of the mushroom cooking—that’s to be expected and just keep going until it evaporates. (3) Don’t forget to reserve plenty of pasta cooking liquid, which is critical to the eventual sauce’s success. I prefer transferring the al dente noodles from the pasta pot to the skillet, letting any residual water come with it (and to ensure you don’t accidentally drain away that liquid gold).

Find more fall favorite meals here: Weeknight Pumpkin Chili; Cream-ish of Mushroom Soup; Mushrooms au Poivre.

Cook 12 oz. egg-based pasta (such as fettuccine nests) in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 1 minute less than package directions.

Meanwhile, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over high. Add 1 lb. crimini or mixed mushrooms (such as button, maitake, oyster, and/or shiitake), sliced ¼" thick or torn into bite-size pieces, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt and toss to coat evenly. Spread out into an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until mushrooms are starting to release their liquid, 2–3 minutes (do not be alarmed; there will be a lot). Continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until moisture is almost completely evaporated and edges of mushrooms are starting to brown, 6–8 minutes.

It has been revealed that reduce heat to medium-high; add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, tossing often, until garlic is fragrant and golden, 1–2 minutes. Pour in ¾ cup dry white wine, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan with a sturdy spatula or flat-edged wooden spoon, and cook until wine is mostly evaporated (you should have about 1 Tbsp. liquid left in pan), about 4 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 2 Tbsp. white miso and stir until melted and combined. Slowly pour in ½ cup heavy cream, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan; simmer until thickened slightly, 2–3 minutes. Add 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce; season with freshly ground pepper. Taste and add more salt if needed.

Recent findings suggest that using tongs, transfer pasta to mushroom mixture and add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Increase heat to medium and bring to a simmer. Cook, tossing constantly and adding ½–1 cup more pasta cooking liquid to reach desired sauce consistency if needed, until pasta is al dente and liquid has thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.

In a recent development, remove pan from heat. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup) to pasta and toss to combine. Season generously with more pepper; taste and season with more salt if needed.

Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan and pepper.

#19682. Is Zalando’s Upcoming AI Agent a Blueprint for the Future of Retail?

Is Zalando’s Upcoming AI Agent a Blueprint for the Future of Retail?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1839 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What happens when a multibrand fashion retailer starts selling products it doesn’t stock?
  • Zalando is testing the service with premium home and living retailer Westwing.
  • Retailers can join through a relatively simple integration, providing something similar to an affiliate product feed and entering into an additional agreement with Zalando.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What happens when a multibrand fashion retailer starts selling products it doesn’t stock? European e-commerce giant Zalando is joining the AI shopping agent race with aims to let shoppers buy from other retailers through its platform. Its latest offering, Zalando Extended, will use AI agents to complete purchases on customers’ behalf, potentially transforming Zalando into a shopping gateway beyond its own catalog.

Zalando is testing the service with premium home and living retailer Westwing. Its products already appear in Zalando’s search and browsing results, but shoppers currently have to click through to Westwing’s website to buy them. From 2027, Zalando’s AI agent will handle those purchases on customers’ behalf, allowing them to check out without leaving the Zalando app.

Retailers can join through a relatively simple integration, providing something similar to an affiliate product feed and entering into an additional agreement with Zalando. The company has not disclosed what commission or fee, if any, it will earn from these transactions. It's a notable move for a retailer that has spent years building its own assortment and relationships with thousands of brands, from Gucci to Burberry and Jacquemus. But as the likes of OpenAI, Google and Meta race to make general-purpose personal AI agents, the battle is increasingly over who controls the customer relationship, rather than simply who stocks the product.

According to recent reports, zalando’s AI assistant currently helps shoppers purchase from the multibrand retailer’s product catalogue. Photo: Courtesy of Zalando.

It has been revealed that zalando’s response is to position itself on both sides of that coin. Its three-pronged strategy aims to make its own platform the first stop for fashion discovery, expand its assortment through external retailers and also reach shoppers through third-party AI agents. It aims to offer checkout within Google’s AI Mode and Gemini app when its agentic commerce releases in Europe, and has tested advertising inside ChatGPT in the UK.

Sources indicate that this also places Zalando in competition with specialist AI shopping platforms such as Daydream, which also launched a upcoming AI shopping agent this week. Both are betting that fashion requires expertise beyond that of general-purpose AI agents. While Daydream operates in the US and Zalando in Europe, the latter enters the race with a significant advantage in scale.

But for rival luxury and multibrand fashion retailers, Zalando’s AI strategy raises a bigger question: is the future of fashion e-commerce about selling your own assortment, or becoming the gateway to everyone else’s?

At the Web Summit conference in Lisbon, Vogue Business sat down with chief technology officer Graeme Smith to discuss the company’s ambitions and who stands to own the customer relationship in the age of AI agents.

Vogue: Why allow Zalando customers to buy products from other retailers through Zalando Extended?

Smith: We’ve got over 63 million active customers at Zalando, and through our Lifestyle AI [Zalando’s umbrella term for its AI-powered personalization technology], we’ve really got to know their preferences — the brands they like, the price points they shop at, the brand values like sustainability they look for, and how their needs change over time. We can use all this to create a personalized experience that can even become proactive.

So we thought, why limit ourselves? We already have our wholesale and partner platforms, but with AI agents, we’ve found a really lightweight way to bring in other retailers whose products you wouldn’t normally find on Zalando.

Our first partner is Westwing. Today, you can discover its products on Zalando and click through to buy them on Westwing. But early next year, you’ll be able to buy that sofa or lamp directly on Zalando, using your existing account and payment details, without leaving the app. We’ll buy it on your behalf.

Imagine how much more assortment across fashion and lifestyle we could offer this way, without stocking it ourselves. We can then build that into our personalization, learning more about customers’ interests beyond our existing catalog and helping them discover more products.

Industry observers note that vogue: With general-purpose AI agents increasingly capable of shopping on consumers’ behalf, are you competing directly with the likes of OpenAI, Google and Meta? Why would shoppers choose Zalando instead?

It has been revealed that people are going to use a variety of agents, but our mission is always to make Zalando the best place to start the fashion and lifestyle shopping journey. That comes down to the customer experience we can provide that others can’t, which starts with data.

We’ve been using AI for over 15 years, including for personalized shopping recommendations, and we’ve invested heavily in size and fit. We get tens of thousands of body measurements a week, and we have so much data from customer returns about which items run small or large. So we’ve got over 10,000 size charts, and we’ve put AI on top of that. No third-party agent has got that. So if you care about getting the fit right the first time, Zalando’s agent will be the place to come.

We’ve also invested in recommending whole outfits based on our understanding of trends, how people shop for different occasions and years of customer behavior at scale.

Vogue: How quickly do you expect Zalando Extended to grow? Are you planning to onboard lots more retailers in the coming months, or is this more of a test-and-learn phase?

It’s a little bit of both. We’re testing and learning, but it’s not a particularly complex thing we’re doing, and we’re very excited by what we’ve seen so far. Assuming it’s successful, this has the potential to scale very fast because the integration is so lightweight.

Most of these retailers already produce an affiliate feed, which is essentially what we need. We can make the sign-up and operations very simple for them, and it’s very light for us too. So there’s potential to scale this massively.

Recent findings suggest that vogue: Trust is fundamental to AI agent adoption, and attitudes vary between markets. Why would consumers trust Zalando Assistant more than a general-purpose AI agent?

It has been revealed that zalando is a brand that people trust, and we’ve worked very hard to earn that trust. The company has just turned 18, and we’ve built that trust through how we look after the customer experience, including how we handle their data. We’re a European company, so the data we hold is subject to high European standards for data protection.

We’ve seen customers enthusiastically adopt Zalando Assistant. Interestingly, questions about what we know about them haven’t been a big part of the conversation — people have just started using it. We’ve had 22 million customers engage with Zalando Assistant this year, including 13 million in the last quarter.

Recent findings suggest that customers are twice as likely to buy something in a session where they use Zalando Assistant compared with one where they don’t. And of course, we have all the consent mechanisms required in Europe. Customers can also request that their data be deleted.

According to recent reports, graeme Smith, Zalando’s CTO. Photo: Courtesy of Zalando.

Vogue: Is there a risk that Zalando could lose its direct relationship with customers by bringing other retailers onto its platform?

It has been revealed that no, we don’t think of it like that. We want people to come to Zalando more and more, and for it to be the place where they start their shopping journey. We’ve got 70% organic traffic, which is very high, and we work hard to maintain that.

We think we can do that by building really great experiences tailored to fashion and lifestyle shopping. Bringing in more retailers actually gives people more reasons to come to Zalando, because they know they can access a wider variety of products. They can buy a sofa on Zalando, as well as everything else. So we think this could actually drive more traffic.

Now, could someone go directly to Westwing to buy their next sofa? Of course, and that’s fine. We don’t sell sofas on Zalando. What matters is that we’re the best place to discover fashion and lifestyle products, wherever they come from.

Vogue: You’re also piloting advertising in ChatGPT and preparing to participate in Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol. How does that fit with your ambition to make Zalando the starting point for shopping?

There are three strands to our strategy. The first is getting people to keep coming back to Zalando as the best place to start their shopping journey. The second is what we call inbound agentic commerce, and the third is Zalando Extended, which allows us to massively expand the assortment available through outbound agentic commerce.

It has been revealed that inbound agentic commerce is what most people talk about when they discuss AI shopping agents. People are using ChatGPT, Google’s AI-powered search and other platforms. We had to decide early on how we felt about that, and we saw it as an opportunity. Our customers are going to use these services anyway, so we want Zalando to be there and meet them where they are. We also want to reach latest customers.

We’ve become very good at generative engine optimisation (GEO) — we’re the number one fashion destination in Europe referred to by AI agents. But we haven’t stopped at organic visibility. We’ve also piloted advertising inside ChatGPT in the UK, and we’re now looking at the results and deciding where to go next.

According to recent reports, with Google, it’s even more interesting. When Google launches agentic commerce in Europe, Zalando will be there from the start. Customers will be able to discover Zalando products and even check out within Google if they want to.

But they’ll still need a Zalando account. That’s very key to us. We want to engage with these AI platforms on our own terms and maintain the customer relationship.

According to recent reports, vogue: Fashion shopping is often emotional and highly considered. Do you think consumers will really want to complete purchases through AI agents, rather than visiting a retailer’s website?

In a recent development, we don’t know how this is going to play out. I’m very excited by it, but fashion is very personal and emotional.

What we see is that when customers arrive at Zalando from another channel, whether that’s an AI agent, Instagram or TikTok, they often don’t buy the item they landed on. They explore three or four more products, look at similar items and browse around before making a purchase.

In a recent development, it’s another signal that fashion is different, it’s a high-consideration purchase. So if I had to bet — and it’s always difficult to make predictions — I think people will use agents to research products, but they’ll still want to click through to the retailer, like Zalando, to ask: is this item quite right for me? What more can I learn about it? What similar products are available? And then maybe they’ll buy from there, but let’s see.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Throughout the years-long process of casting the new James Bond, I tried to follow the watches to an answer. When Aaron Taylor-Johnson joined the Omega family in May 2025, it felt like watching the 007 Vatican spit white smoke from its steeple. Just this past weekend, fans were still pinning red strings on their bulletin boards between Jack Lowden and the MI6 superspy when images resurfaced of the Slow Horses star wearing Omega. Since 1995’s Goldeneye, Bond has been an Omega man—a relationship later canonized in one of cinema’s most iconic line readings, when Daniel Craig confirmed his brand of choice in three stretched-out syllables: Oh-Mee-Guh.

Sources indicate that if, like me, you were only basing your predictions on what the reported pool of potential Bonds wore on their wrists, Robert Pattinson would have been an easy name to cross off. The newly declared 007 only signed on as an ambassador for the Swiss luxury brand Jaeger-LeCoultre two short months ago! When I interviewed Pattinson about the appointment over the summer, he was effusive about his new partner: “I very rarely even wear watches, but when I tried it on, I was like, ‘That’s my favorite watch.’ I wanted to just buy it.”.

Now, in addition to juggling his other iconic role as Batman, Pattinson will presumably need to balance his existing commitment to JLC with his fresh gig’s long-held ties to Omega. (Reps for both brands did not immediately respond to requests for comment, though JLC conspicuously posted a photo of Pattinson on Instagram a few hours after the announcement.).

During our conversation earlier this summer, Pattinson revealed what he looks for in a watch. He caught the collecting bug in March, when he wore JLC’s Master Control Chronometre Perpetual Calendar to the Oscars afterparties. “All these other actors with their fancy watches on asked me, ‘Hey, what are you wearing?’” Pattinson recalls. “It was one of those moments where I’m like, ‘It’s kind of badass having this thing on.’”.

Sources indicate that if it’s attention-grabbing badass watches Pattinson is after, he’s in good hands with Omega. The brand is best known for supplying the watches Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin wore when they landed on the moon in 1969. Omega has been happy to create special versions of the Speedmaster for its current partners to dial up its profile. And, of course, the Swiss house continues to expand its Bond-inspired offerings: The maker recently added a “Spectre” version of the Seamaster, 007’s preferred model, to the lineup. And whenever Omega needs to drum up buzz around soon-to-be-released models, they tend to show up on former Bond Craig’s wrists during public appearances.

Sources indicate that speculators trying to pin down the next Bond would have had better luck if they’d read some less recent watch tea leaves. Back in 2020, Christopher Nolan released Tenet, his inscrutable but enthralling time-warp thriller in which Pattinson plays a mysterious, dapper, and charming spy involved in a high-stakes mission to save the world—about as good a preview of what the 40-year-old actor will look like as 007 as you’ll find in his filmography. And the watch on his wrist in that flick? An Omega.

Cider-Braised Sausage and Lentils

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • More great fall recipes this way: Charred Cabbage With Sausages and Apples; Pork Chops With Green Chiles and Apples; Mustardy Cider-Braised Pork Chops.
  • extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I haven’t made a meal in the French countryside in fall; but sometimes I dream, and these slow-cooked lentils are what I’d make in such a situation. Back in my American reality, it still makes an excellent dinner or hearty weekend lunch. Look for mild smoked Austrian or German sausages, which lean on mellow herbs and warm spices (sometimes, if you’re lucky, they’re also stuffed with a nutty cheese)—this style is already cooked to a safe temperature, but the casing’s texture is greatly improved when seared before reheating. If your shop only carries sweet Italian sausage or something like an apple-stuffed chicken sausage, both work in a pinch. What a treat it will be to actually finish off that gallon of apple cider you impulsively bought last week in the lentil-braising liquid.

More great fall recipes this way: Charred Cabbage With Sausages and Apples; Pork Chops With Green Chiles and Apples; Mustardy Cider-Braised Pork Chops.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.), turning often, until deeply browned on all sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Combine 1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped, 3 celery stalks, finely chopped, 1 large carrot, peeled, finely chopped, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in same pan. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring often and scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring, just until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add 2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 1½ cups apple cider, 1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed, ½ cup finely chopped parsley, 3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to pan. Increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Cover pan, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook until lentils are tender and most of the liquid is absorbed but mixture is still saucy, 30–35 minutes.

Sources indicate that uncover pan and stir in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar. Nestle sausages into lentil mixture and add any juices pooled on plate. Simmer until sausages are warmed through, about 5 minutes. Top with parsley leaves and reserved celery leaves to serve.

#19678. Daydream’s New AI Agent Can Shop for You While You Sleep

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2146 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vogue ↗ Open Full Page

Daydream’s New AI Agent Can Shop for You While You Sleep

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2146 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that daydream wants to become a personal stylist in your pocket.
  • In a recent development, the new agent, which shoppers can chat with through Daydream’s app or by texting it directly via SMS, marks an evolution from the conversational fashion search engine the company rolled out just over a year ago.
  • During an exclusive preview, co-founder and chief brand officer Lisa Yamner asks the agent to resume shopping for an upcoming trip to Mexico.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that daydream wants to become a personal stylist in your pocket. The AI-powered fashion discovery platform, launched in 2025 by former Stitch Fix executive Julie Bornstein, is introducing a 24/7 AI shopping agent that can learn consumers’ tastes, assemble outfits and purchase products on their behalf — even while they sleep.

In a recent development, the new agent, which shoppers can chat with through Daydream’s app or by texting it directly via SMS, marks an evolution from the conversational fashion search engine the company rolled out just over a year ago. It can remember previous exchanges, put together complete outfits, offer virtual try-ons using an uploaded photograph and handle the steps leading up to checkout.

During an exclusive preview, co-founder and chief brand officer Lisa Yamner asks the agent to resume shopping for an upcoming trip to Mexico. Remembering her aims, it asks a few questions before assembling looks for beachfront dinners, complete with dresses, shoes and bags. Yamner swaps between pieces, tries them on using a virtual version of herself and uploads an influencer’s Instagram image to find similar items.

“Once you express a need or an interest, it can shop while you sleep,” Yamner explains. Shoppers can leave the agent to monitor products for price drops or continue working on a shopping request in the background, rather than repeatedly checking themselves. Any purchase still requires their approval. “We firmly believe that shopping doesn’t have to be a task, but there are parts of it that become that.” The aim is to take the drudgery out of shopping without losing the pleasure of discovery, she says.

At launch, the agent can shop across Daydream’s existing network of roughly 350 brand and retail partners, spanning more than 10,000 brands and three million products. Shoppers can ask it to purchase an item on their behalf, or check out directly with the retailer.

It has been revealed that it comes as OpenAI, Instinct and Meta double down on shopping as a core use case and revenue stream for their newly introduced ‘always on’ agents, and fashion retailers are now racing to build their own agents. Last week, Zalando revealed plans for an AI agent that will purchase products on customers’ behalf from other retailers as well as its own catalog, from 2027. Meanwhile, brands including Ralph Lauren and J.Crew are building out their own branded AI shopping assistants, with J.Crew partnering with Anthropic on its upcoming AI “Style Advisor”. Last month, Prada became the first luxury brand to launch an official plugin within OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

Industry observers note that daydream's answer is to sell its fashion expertise. The firm has developed an internal “fashion knowledge graph” to enrich the information attached to products in its catalog, while human stylists help shape the agent’s recommendations. It recently appointed Francesca Sully as its first “stylist in residence”, tasked with teaching the technology to think more like a stylist and keep pace with trends.

Recent findings suggest that daydream recently appointed Francesca Sully as its first “stylist in residence”, tasked with teaching the AI agent to think more like a human stylist and keep pace with trends. Photo: Courtesy of Daydream.

Sources indicate that its founders believe a general-purpose AI agent, however sophisticated, will struggle to replicate the nuances of personal style. It comes back to the central question haunting fashion AI: can it mimic taste?

“We feel like a generalized agent is just not going to get fashion right,” Bornstein tells Vogue Business in an exclusive interview alongside co-founder Lisa Yamner. “Style is so nuanced. It relates to some very specific things that matter. So we need to know the right questions to ask, but also understand the product catalog of every brand out there — not just the price points, but also what the aesthetic of a brand world is, and how to connect that to other brands that align with that aesthetic and may be of interest.”.

It has been revealed that that expertise is also intended to help shoppers discover unfamiliar labels: approximately 97% of searches on Daydream contain no brand name, according to Bornstein. But in an increasingly crowded market, can that fashion expertise stand up as an independent AI shopping offering against the mass convenience of frontier AI agents and trusted retailers’ owned product catalogs?

Recent findings suggest that when Daydream debuted last year, its proposition was to solve one of fashion e-commerce’s enduring frustrations: finding the right product across a fragmented universe of brands and retailers. Its conversational search engine allowed shoppers to describe what they wanted in natural language, rather than relying on conventional keywords and filters, encouraging owners to “say more” about what they sought.

Although Daydream had already positioned itself around the idea of an AI agent, what it lacked was the ability to deliver the more involved, personalized service its founders envisaged — agents in their current form didn’t actually exist.

“We’ve been wanting to build from day one, but it took us a while to get there for a couple of reasons: one was that the agentic technology wasn’t yet there, and two is that the first version of the platform helped us really understand what consumers were looking for and what they wanted from an AI shopping assistant,” Bornstein notes, explaining that Daydream was finding its original product couldn’t deliver the level of assistance shoppers wanted. Shoppers were asking very specific questions to find products for a need that included an occasion and their body type, and Daydream was showing them a page of search results, “when what they really wanted was more tailored help,” Bornstein adds. Conversational search might make finding fashion products easier, but it doesn’t necessarily solve the more subjective problem of deciding what to wear.

Bornstein recalls a similar challenge at her previous firm, The Yes, where shoppers struggled to move beyond the conventions of traditional search. “We tried to get people to search by telling us a need and they would say, ‘Oh, I need a red dress for a Valentine’s Day party. I want to look sexy, but age-appropriate.’ And then you’d say, ‘Great, go ahead and type it into the search part.’ But then they would type in ‘red dress’, because their trust in search working was so low, and there was no mental model of being able to give a more detailed prompt.”.

ChatGPT helped change that behavior, she says, making consumers more comfortable describing their needs in detail — and helping people understand how to use a product like Daydream. “Consumer expectations have started to change and people now understand what an agent is in a way they definitely didn’t two years ago when we started and no one understood what we were talking about,” Bornstein says.

In a recent development, the platform indicates it has amassed more than 2 million customers since its June 2025 launch, with millennial women its largest audience, followed by Gen X and Gen Z. Bornstein describes two overlapping groups: fashion-savvy shoppers who appreciate having thousands of brands in one place, and time-poor consumers seeking more direction. But Daydream won’t disclose how many of its 2 million shoppers return or make purchases, making it difficult to gauge whether initial curiosity is translating into increased sales.

According to recent reports, it comes just a week after Zalando revealed an adjacent offering — a fresh AI agent feature, Zalando Extended, that will allow shoppers to discover and buy products from other third-party retailers without leaving the Zalando app, available from 2027. The European multibrand platform has 63 million active customers, extensive brand relationships and years of purchase and sizing data — assets that a much younger shopping platform like Daydream can’t easily replicate. Yet Bornstein argues the two companies are targeting different markets — Zalando solely operates in Europe, while Daydream is focused solely on the US. She also says the US retail landscape’s department stores and multibrand retailers generally have “more curated assortments”.

“The fact Zalando is going outside its own catalog makes a lot of sense because they’ve always tried to be extremely broad and like the higher-end ‘Amazon of fashion’ in Europe,” Bornstein argues.

But geography offers only a partial defence in a market where frontier AI models like ChatGPT and Claude are developing shopping capabilities that could eventually reach consumers across multiple countries, and gain more sophisticated fashion knowledge, via direct brand plugins like ChatGPT’s recently launched Prada plugin.

Asked what Daydream can offer that a much larger retailer can’t, Bornstein points to its first-mover advantage as the first cross-brand conversational search tool that’s “properly entrenched in fashion”, and the two years of data and prompts it’s collected from fashion-savvy consumers in that time. “I would also say we are solely focused on this,” she adds. “Having worked for other larger companies before in my past, I know how hard it is to build something like this on the side.”.

Recent findings suggest that there is also competition from fashion brands themselves. Ralph Lauren’s Ask Ralph and the launch of J.Crew’s fresh AI stylist last week suggest that brands increasingly want to provide personalized guidance within their own shopping environments.

Recent findings suggest that yet Bornstein says these brand-owned stylists can sit alongside Daydream’s ambitions. “When we launched originally, many brands asked us if we could build this AI agent for their sites,” she says. “And what we said to them is our initial goal is to have one place for consumers to go and see all brands — without having 10 tabs open.”.

Daydream has also expanded into providing its technology to brands. Around eight brand sites are currently using its conversational search technology, Yamner says, and the company plans to bring some of its newly introduced agentic capabilities to those partners.

Recent findings suggest that “Our feeling is if you know the brand and you go straight to the brand, there’s no reason why you wouldn’t want tools to help you shop that brand as effectively as you can,” Bornstein says. “So we’ll evolve the agentic product that we provide to brand sites to map to our core product, as it’s very portable to single brands too. But we are fundamentally focused on the B2C experience — it just also happens to work for B2B.”.

One of Daydream’s potentially most valuable assets is the information it gathers from the way consumers describe their shopping needs. Traditional e-commerce search data might tell a brand that shoppers are searching for dresses or shoes. Conversational search can reveal the occasion, aesthetic and practical requirements behind those searches, as well as details like whether shoppers are searching for particular past collaborations or archive pieces — valuable data for brands’ product development and merchandising decisions, Bornstein indicates.

But the next stage of its personalization strategy requires shoppers to share considerably more. Daydream is developing integrations with Gmail and Google Calendar so its new AI agent can access this customer data and allow it to identify upcoming occasions and learn about previous purchases and marketing email subscriptions. Shoppers will soon also be able to share Pinterest boards with the agent to communicate their style preferences.

It has been revealed that users can set Daydream’s upcoming AI agent tasks, like price comparison and stock checks, that it can carry out 24/7, even while they sleep. Photo: Courtesy of Daydream.

The pitch is that Daydream’s AI stylist would therefore know what’s already in a shopper's wardrobe and make more relevant recommendations. But granting a commercial shopping platform access to emails and calendar information is a significant privacy decision. Consumers will need to understand exactly what Daydream can access, how that information is used and what control they retain over it.

In a recent development, daydream also operates on a commission model, yet Bornstein insists that commercial relationships won’t influence what the agent recommends — and it’s not pursuing advertising within the agent, at least for now. “There are no commercial incentives that go into what highlights up for the customer,” she says. “Whatever they buy, we receive the same level of commission. So we are completely agnostic in what we’re showing and it’s about the customer’s preferences.” Brands will continue to receive customer information when purchases are completed through Daydream.

Recent findings suggest that while Daydream is investing in a more complex and personalized experience, it’s not disclosed the conversion or retention figures needed to assess how effectively that experience translates into repeat purchasing. But Bornstein and Yamner remain convinced that fashion requires a different approach from the general-purpose agents increasingly being developed to manage everyday tasks.

“We’re watching the direction that the tech and customers are moving in, and we’re trying to get out ahead of it,” Yamner indicates. “We’re trying to say we get it. We get that this is what the customer’s expectations are going to become.”.

  • Recent findings suggest that duchovny went on to star in Californication, a raunchy dramedy about a divorced novelist navigating the sexually and professionally parasitic Hollywood studio system of the 2000s.
  • It has been revealed that in addition to his six books, Duchovny has released four records, and written and directed a number of feature films.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Duchovny has been famous for as long as I have been alive. From 1993 to 2002, The X-Files made government conspiracies a staple of primetime television. Duchovny’s FBI special agent Fox Mulder, with his skeptical counterpart, Gillian Anderson’s agent Dana Scully, personified the imminent breakdown of consensus reality in the coming century, delivering the paranoid fringe into 20 million American living rooms. The show belongs to a world of monoculture that no longer exists, and it released Duchovny into a realm of visibility that’s hard to imagine now, when famous people are produced and consumed at an industrial rate. A few weeks ago, as my boyfriend shopped for a suit jacket at Crowley Vintage in Brooklyn and I edited this story on my phone, I watched a college-age boy put on a long, gray trench coat and announce to his girlfriend: “Mulder mode.”.

Recent findings suggest that duchovny went on to star in Californication, a raunchy dramedy about a divorced novelist navigating the sexually and professionally parasitic Hollywood studio system of the 2000s. Many viewers interpreted Californication as a kind of autofiction, although Duchovny did not write for the show. The actor has written a number of novels, but it’s apparent to anyone who has spent 30 seconds with him that this soft-spoken, reluctant celebrity has nothing to do with the character Hank Moody. Still, Californication did anticipate something about art, celebrity, and self-commodification: Anybody who writes today must contend with marketing an artistic persona for a public that does not, as a rule, read.

It has been revealed that in addition to his six books, Duchovny has released four records, and written and directed a number of feature films. He greets the degraded state of American arts with a charming blend of rigor and self-deprecation. “I’m not Jonathan Franzen,” he says of his fiction-writing process. “But if I work on something every day, it deepens. And eventually, hopefully, I can achieve one tenth of what Jonathan Franzen achieves.” But he has an aversion to the sort of publicity that might make his various artistic ventures more lucrative. He tells me he finds it “spiritually impoverishing.”.

I meet Duchovny with his band—millennial slackers half his age—at their practice space in Carroll Gardens, where they’re preparing to tour their fourth LP, Prince of Pieces. He wears a white Hanes T-shirt, tight underneath his athletic arms, and he has a tattoo on his ankle—a compass pointing west, something he got when his daughter, West, was hospitalized as an infant. (She’s 27 now, an accomplished actor. “She wanted to be a doctor,” he indicates. “I was so happy when she told me she was going to pursue acting. Thank God.”).

It has been revealed that the albums are composed of subdued, easy-to-listen-to folk-rock tracks, not dissimilar from early Kurt Vile. It’s the band’s first rehearsal in ages, and one of their only chances to prepare in advance of a European tour. In person, they play the songs harder and heavier, sprinkling in crowd-pleasing covers: “Godzilla” by Blue Öyster Cult, “The One I Love” by REM, and—“sadly only one time,” Duchovny states—“Hotline Bling.” The energy in the room is high. These men like one another. Duchovny’s manager offers me a beer from the cooler I’m perched on. I gesture to the tallboy in my purse. He looks disappointed. “You didn’t trust us,” he says. Duchovny steps aside to take a sip of water and picks up the microphone.

“You can sing along,” his keyboardist, Colin Lee, says.

“I can sing along?” Duchovny asks.

Duchovny at rehearsal with his band.

Sources indicate that at 66, David Duchovny remains a sex symbol. He’s in better shape than he was on The X-Files. He’s in better shape than the boys in the band. The night after practice, during a Q&A for a screening of his 2023 film Reverse the Curse, he mentions that the wardrobe department had to fashion a “BDSM harness” for him to wear under his clothes to remind him to hunch like an old man. He plays a Red Sox fan who bonds with his estranged son over baseball, marijuana, and their shared lust for a beautiful, young death doula. Duchovny’s character has terminal cancer. “I’m in my dying era,” he tells the crowd. “I die in every film. ”.

For the most part, the audience at Westchester County’s Irvington Theater is old enough to have watched The X-Files as it aired. At least two esoteric-looking old men carry David’s poetry collection like a prayer book. There are a handful of young people. A college-aged girl in a KN95 mask raises her hand to ask about Bucky Fucking Dent, the novel adaptation of the Reverse the Curse screenplay, which Duchovny wrote while the movie was in production purgatory. “In the book, Ted and Marty’s last name is Fullilove. In the movie you change it to Fullaker. Why did you do that?”.

Industry observers note that “Good question,” Duchovny says, stalling. “Full of love. Full of shit. It’s all the same.”.

Inevitably, someone asks about the new X-Files. Ryan Coogler is rebooting the show for Hulu. Duchovny will later suggest to me that Chris Carter, the show’s original writer, has designs on a reboot of his own—“He has plans, and wants to end with the original show.” As for Coogler’s version, he states, “I know he said he wants me to come do something, but we haven’t figured out what yet.” During the audience Q&A, Duchovny seems to have misheard the question, and spoils the ending for The Exiles, his forthcoming Taiwanese crime film: “I die in that one too.”.

Duchovny’s latest book, About Time, a collection of poems published last year by Akashic, is also largely about dying: the death of his father, the death of his first marriage, the ambient death that hung in the air at the beginning of the decade. He started writing the poems when his therapist encouraged him to talk to dead people. “He was talking about Rudolph Steiner’s belief that you can talk to the dead. And he said: You can talk to your father and you should. My dad and I didn’t connect like we might have,” Duchovny claims. “When you’re younger, you think you have all the time in the world to get the relationship you want. But the relationship doesn’t end.” In conversation, he is cerebral without being annoying. “There’s a power struggle when you read a really good novel,” he says. “Somebody’s mind is taking over your mind. I think about language a lot and how we take it for granted as being an accurate signifier. When I was younger I thought communication was possible. I’m not so sure now. But it’s fun to try.”.

Recent findings suggest that duchovny’s humility complicates the sexual charisma that still lives at the center of his public persona. His introduction to About Time begins, “I know what you’re thinking: Just what the world needs now—a bunch of poems from an actor.” There’s a sense that he wants to get ahead of the reader’s skepticism. But there’s also plenty of perceptive lines in the poems themselves: “You dreamt you wrote something so good, / so ambivalent and destructive, so creative, / so lacking in morals, decency, or instruction, / so sad and so funny, / so useless and old, / so familiar and newly introduced, / so full of theft and power / that they had to name a god after it.” I ask him if good writing is necessarily amoral. He indicates, “Probably. Which is why any politically correct work of art is usually super successful and really bad. Usually artists are difficult people, and I have no problem separating the art from the artist. But people do now.”.

In a recent development, in college, Duchovny wanted to be a poet. “I thought it was an actual occupation you could have,” he says. When an underclassman turned up in his workshop who was better than him, he quit writing poems on the spot. “It was actually Walter Kirn,” he says. “He showed up at 16-years-old. He was a genius. I was like okay—I’m not a poet.”.

The two men have become close in the last decade. Kirn, who wrote Up in the Air and founded the newspaper County Highway, tells me what Duchovny was like at Princeton: “He was golden. He had an aura. I was a little starstruck by him.” Duchovny has agreed to play paranormal radio host Art Bell in American Nights, a biopic that Kirn is developing alongside director Alex Lee Moyer. Bell’s Coast to Coast, a cult AM show during the ’80s and ’90s, was beloved by long-haul truckers and compound preppers alike, who called in to report UFO sightings, cattle mutilations, and crop circles. “I, like the rest of my generation, grew up on The X-Files,” Moyer tells me. “It made a massive impression on me, and I’ve been a fan of David ever since. The synchronicity of him being a part of this is not lost on me.”.

I ask Duchovny if he always needed to be the best. “I at least needed to be the best in my class,” he says.

In LA, I meet Duchovny in a quiet restaurant to talk about his books. He describes his first novel as “an act of cowardice.” Holy Cow is narrated by an anthropomorphized barnyard animal who uncovers the conspiracy theory that is factory farming. “I thought: Well, they’re not gonna cut me off at the knees on this. Because I’m clearly not that serious. It was calculated. I didn’t want to try for the great American novel the first time as an actor.” The books that followed are more ambitious, each one better than the last. By the time he was promoting his fourth book, 2021’s Truly Like Lightning, he made his ambition plain. “I want to be taken seriously,” he said on Marc Maron’s podcast. “That’s my weakness. I want that book to be taken seriously.”.

“You don’t want people to be like the guy from The X-Files wrote a book,” Maron said.

“That’s what they’re gonna say,” Duchovny said, “but I hope and I believe that eventually people will see that I mean business.”.

In a recent development, truly Like Lightning centers on a Mormon polygamist family forced to enter the godless world of Los Angeles when their homestead is upended. “When I started to read about Mormonism, it struck me as super optimistic. Everyone’s gonna get their own planet and everyone’s gonna be able to propagate souls. As opposed to a European perspective, which was always about the end of something, being 2,000 years removed from this thing. The Mormons noted no, this is still happening.” The novel takes cues from the literary critic Harold Bloom, who wrote that Mormonism was an “American original” and called its founder a “religious genius.” Duchovny studied under Bloom at Yale, where he earned some of an English PhD. “Everything goes back to Bloom,” he says. “And you never really leave grad school. I’m not sure I’ve left grad school. They might still be waiting for my dissertation.”.

But Duchovny did leave grad school. He signed with a talent agent one summer to try to earn some money acting in commercials. His agent told him that if he wanted to go out for theater or film roles, he’d have to get into an acting class. “I stated: I’m not doing anything. When I stepped into acting class, something happened. I wasn’t a demonstrative person—I was an intellectual person. So it was like: Yeah, be unreasonable. Be irrational. It opened up a different world, a world of fiction, a world without consequences. I’m doing a scene, and I’m yelling at this person and I’m going to murder them, but I don’t have to go to jail.”.

For someone with half a dozen good books and an enormous public profile, it’s surprising there haven’t been more reviews. Johnny Temple, who published Duchovny’s two most recent books on Akashic, tells me, “It’s certainly frustrating that there hasn't been more review coverage of David’s books. For any well-known actor, musician, or other type of public figure, there’s always going to be obstacles to being taken seriously in a different medium.” Kirn tells me, “That makes writing fiction a much purer achievement in my mind. You’re doing this because you love it, and you know that two thirds of your fans will only remember you as a TV character. It’s a brilliant, Sisyphean task. Also, he’s a superb writer.”.

I ask Duchovny whether he still thinks about being the best. “I think now I can acknowledge that it’s a hollow designation,” he says. “Especially in the arts. Even though we give awards, which is silly. Holy Cow made the Times bestseller list. Ever since, everything I write sells less and less.”.

Industry observers note that “It’s hard for someone to champion it,” he adds. “If I wrote a memoir, I’m sure it would get reviewed in the Times.”.

Industry observers note that talking to Duchovny, one is reminded that wanting to be taken seriously and being in on the joke aren’t mutually exclusive. As band practice winds down in Brooklyn, the guys are excited to cover Lou Reed’s “Perfect Day.” Duchovny crosses his arms in front of his lap like a schoolboy as he sings. To my ear it sounds just fine, but Lee, the keyboardist, asks the mixer to lower the reverb on David’s voice.

“Maybe lower David’s mic in general?” the bassist, Mitchell Stewart asks.

“Lower than zero,” Duchovny states. “Less than zero.”.

A few days later, he texts me. He just screened an early cut of Soapbox, a Hollywood satire he wrote and stars in opposite Laverne Cox. At first, he’s bummed that the test audience has decided that his character shouldn’t get killed in the final moments of the movie. But a couple hours later, he writes me again: “People don’t want me to die. I guess I should be flattered.”.

From Sean Connery’s immaculately tailored suits in Dr. No to Daniel Craig’s thigh-bearing trunks in Casino Royale, each man who has played James Bond has brought a new aesthetic sensibility to the role. For Connery, this meant soft-shouldered Savile Row tailoring, polo shirts, and knit ties to suit the era of Ivy Style, while Roger Moore’s wardrobe of safari jackets and nylon ski suits embodied the sporty hedonism of the 1970s. In the 21st century, Daniel Craig’s Bond was built around a timely blend of Brioni, Tom Ford, and stalwart British brands that complemented the contemporary #menswear scene. Today’s news that Robert Pattinson—a longtime Dior ambassador and one of the most consistently thrilling dressers in Hollywood—has been cast as 007 suggests Bond’s most fashionable era may be yet to come.

In a recent development, daniel Craig is no slouch in the clothing department, but before donning the tux for Casino Royale, he was primarily known as a stage actor with a penchant for distressed jeans and Chuck Taylor high-tops. Pattinson, meanwhile, has been the face of Dior’s menswear for a decade, during which he’s established his impeccable taste and a willingness to take major swings with his outfits—not to mention a reputation for wearing the absolute heck out of a gray suit. Now, with fellow Brit Jonathan Anderson (who cast Craig in Loewe’s quirked-up fall 2024 campaign and posted this heartwarming pic today) running the show at Dior, the stage is set for a Bond with a taste for capital-F fashion.

Sources indicate that tradition dictates a vibe shift whenever a new Bond is chosen, but whatever James Bond wears has an outsized impact on menswear. Pierce Brosnan’s era had structured Brioni suits and made the Omega Seamaster a star, while Daniel Craig helped cement Tom Ford’s tailoring as a red-carpet staple and juiced sales of N.Peal ribbed Army sweaters and Drake’s suede chukkas. As GQ’s Cam Wolf noted in a 2018 article about Skyfall, Daniel Craig’s Barbour jacket, sweater, jeans, and brogue boots from that film—a classic but fairly unremarkable outfit—became the aspirational template for untold numbers of men on r/malefashionadvice. A few years later, when Craig wore a Rag & Bone slim-fit henley in No Time to Die, the brand sold out of the unassuming undershirt in a matter of days.

It’s been five years since No Time to Die’s release, and it will likely be at least a couple more before Pattinson’s first outing as 007 hits screens. That’s a long wait to see how the next Bond era aesthetic comes together, but given Pattinson’s distinctive approach to fashion, it should be well worth it for the clothes alone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a big, bold piece of protein. Case in point: This salty-sweet salmon glazed in a glossy teriyaki-style sauce. Brushed in two rounds with the quick sauce made with nothing more than sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vinegar, the salmon sizzles under the broiler, charring as it takes on a smoky flavor. This recipe calls for one large piece of salmon, but you can use smaller fillets or opt for a white fish such as cod or halibut. Just note that the cooking time will be shorter if using smaller pieces, so keep an eye on them. Add a quick garnish of sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds, and dinner is done.

More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.

Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

Heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving. Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.).

Broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that richard Avedon spent decades shooting for magazines like Vogue, Harper’s Bazaar, and The Fresh Yorker before his death in 2004. Now his life and work are the subjects of a new documentary, Avedon, directed by Ron Howard.

To learn more about Avedon’s legacy—and to hear what it was like to work with him as both a model and a fashion editor—Nicole Phelps invited Tonne Goodman on to The Run-Through.

Goodman was still in high school when she entered the world of fashion. “I was in 10th grade and I wanted a summer intern job,” she explains. What she got, through her friendship with Diana Vreeland’s grandson, was modeling work for Vogue. “I think that the fact that she sent me to Avedon and to Penn and to the best photographers that the magazine had at that point was really a gesture of kindness to her grandson,” Goodman states.

It has been revealed that her first photograph in Vogue, taken by Avedon, was published in 1971. Decades later, she would collaborate with him as an editor on a commercial shoot for Neiman Marcus starring model Nadja Auermann. “Dick was a sponge. He captured every single kind of example of a fashion photograph that you could possibly take,” she says. “I’m sure that there is not a photographer today who has not referenced his work in some way or another.”.

Later in the episode, after the break, Chloe Malle sits down with the film’s director, Ron Howard. At first, he says, the Avedon Foundation was reluctant to open its archives to a documentary crew, but Howard’s 2024 film Jim Henson Idea Man persuaded them that the material would be in safe hands.

In a recent development, as he began the research, Howard says, “I think they could just see that I was pretty blown away. I related to him a lot more than I thought I would. I began to understand that these weren’t snapshots. He wasn’t ever counting on luck—he really was a storyteller.”.

Recent findings suggest that the two also discuss Avedon’s motivations, and some of the unflattering reviews he received during his career. “A lot of interesting people are paradoxes, right? He had that anger that was pushing him,” Howard posits. “We talk about how he was frustrated by the critics. And of course, they were devastating to him in a way, but I think he used that as fuel.”.

Sources indicate that in the end, Tonne believes that Avedon would have appreciated what Avedon has to say about him. “I think Ron got him,” she indicates, “and I think he would’ve gotten it totally.”.

In a food processor, pulse the cream cheese, goat cheese, butter, and garlic powder until the mixture is smooth. Add parsley, chives, and thyme and pulse until well combined. Then season with salt and black pepper.

Transfer the cream cheese mixture to a piece of plastic wrap and gather up the wrap to form a ball. Then transfer the mixture into a large bowl and refrigerate until it’s firm, which should take at least three hours and up to one day.

In a clean food processor, pulse 3/4 cup pecan halves until they are finely chopped.

Transfer the pecans to a plate.

Roll the cheese ball in nuts and arrange it all on a platter.

Start by cutting a large triangle from a red bell pepper—this will be the face. Next, cut a smaller triangle from a yellow bell pepper for the beak. For the eyes, slice two small rounds from a small carrot. Take a larger carrot and slice it into diagonal ovals to make the feet, then carve little triangles at one end to look like toes. Finally, thinly slice the rest of the carrots into matchsticks for the tail.

According to recent reports, grab some toothpicks and stick the carrot eyes onto the red triangle face. Then, use another toothpick to add the yellow beak to the face—just make sure all the toothpicks point toward the back so you can attach everything to the cheese ball later. Now, press the face onto the front of the cheese ball, and slide the carrot feet into the base.

According to recent reports, insert matchstick carrots, pretzel sticks, and mini pretzels into the back of the ball to create the tail. Using the remaining 1/2 cup pecan halves, create wings by overlapping them along each side of the ball. Serve with crackers alongside!

Store leftover cheese ball in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. If possible, remove the pretzels and vegetable decorations before storing, as they can soften over time.
